title: Exit Reason Lexicon and Ops Summary Dashboard
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement an operator-facing "Exit Reason Lexicon" (ERL) and a compact Ops Summary Dashboard that surfaces the dominant exit/rejection modes across the inference stack. The goal is to translate low-level signals (HTTP/gRPC codes, runtime exit modes, model token errors, timeouts, backpressure signals, GPU OOMs) into a small set of actionable categories (e.g., timeout, overload, model-reject, infra-resource, protocol-error) and expose both high-cardinality slices and a triage-first summary for oncall. Work includes: (1) schema for standard failure_reason tags available to traces/metrics/logs; (2) tracehook augmentation in the request adapter to attach ERL metadata; (3) metric pipeline enrichment and rollup rules in the telemetry ingestion layer; (4) log JSON normalization and structured fields for failure reasons; (5) Grafana dashboard panels + drilldowns into Trace Link and Log Explorer. This ticket covers design, proto rollout, initial pipeline implementation, dashboard authoring, and the QA plan for SLO impact measurement.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 for failure_reason documented and approved (Confluence link)
Tracehook adds failure_reason tag for 95% of terminal request traces in canary region
Telemetry pipeline emits aggregated failure_reason counts and SLO exposure metrics
Ops Summary Dashboard shows top 5 exit reasons, percent SLO exposure, and links to representative traces/logs
Runbook snippets for each lexicon category added to oncall playbook
notes: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting — aligned on five primary categories (timeout, overload, model_error, infra_resource, protocol_error). Decided to keep lexicon small to limit cardinality in dashboards.

2026-02-22: Prototype schema submitted; opted for a short enum (failure_reason) + optional failure_subtype freeform field for debugging; trade-off: additional cardinality but preserves investigability.
2026-02-28: Chose to implement tracehook changes in adapter layer rather than runtime core to reduce risk and accelerate rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

2026-03-03: Telemetry team implemented enrichment stage that maps HTTP/gRPC codes + runtime exit markers -> failure_reason. Initial false-positive rate ~4% for model_error due to ambiguous model signal; tracking refinement in mapping rules.
2026-03-07: UX review requested for dashboard layout; PM suggests an 'impact-first' row that orders categories by SLO minutes lost, not raw count. Good for prioritization.

2026-03-09: Canary deployment in us-west-2: tracehook tagging enabled for 10% of traffic. Dashboard panels populated via aggregated metrics; some missing trace links for cached responses — investigating trace correlation ID propagation.
2026-03-10: Decision to add 1-minute rolling sampling for high-cardinality subtypes in production to manage storage costs. Added to rollout plan.
risks: Cardinality explosion if teams add many failure_subtype values — mitigated via sampling + enforced allowlist for subtype in schema v1
Incorrect mapping of model-level soft rejections to model_error can inflate perceived model instability — plan: add a secondary model_signal_score and review edges with Applied ML team
Latency overhead from tracehook enrichment at high QPS — will measure overhead in canary and add asynchronous enrichment path if >2ms median impact
plan: Week 1: Finalize lexicon and Confluence spec. Implement schema in telemetry repo and create test vectors.
Week 2: Implement tracehook changes in adapter; integration tests and unit coverage. Start 10% canary in single region.
Week 3: Telemetry pipeline rollup and dashboard authoring; UX pass with PM/SRE. Tweak mapping rules based on canary data.
Week 4: Gradual global rollout + runbook updates + post-launch monitoring for false positives and storage costs.
